behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent acted as a virtual account manager managing three assigned contacts but chose to actively engage only with R. Patel, who was in week two of a trial. It initiated a proactive outreach to Patel with friendly guidance and an offer for a short walkthrough. After Patel replied, the agent coordinated logistics for a 20-minute session, shared enablement materials (QuickStart, screencast, sample CSV), and set up demo users for safe practice. Across several rounds, it confirmed time zones, meeting time, materials, and demo-account preferences. It did not initiate any contact with the other two assigned customers during the simulation.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns:
The agent displays a moderately extroverted pattern focused deeply on a single relationship rather than broadly across all available contacts. It proactively initiates contact with Patel and repeatedly proposes live interactions (20-minute walkthrough, calendar invite, pre-call checklist), using warm, polite language (“hope week two… going well,” “Thanks — totally understand the timing,” “Perfect — thanks, R.”) and multiple follow-up questions that keep the thread active (availability, email preference, demo user configuration, escalation criteria). Its language is consistently cordial and socially aware but remains concise and task-focused rather than elaborately expressive; it avoids small talk beyond brief well-wishes and appreciation. Social and relational aims are woven into task framing—emphasizing making the team “comfortable,” “practice without touching live data,” and “feel good using this before I make a call”—but the agent does not explicitly highlight relationship-building as a separate, ongoing objective.

Most notably, the agent shows a strong tendency to sustain and deepen the ongoing interaction with Patel over several turns, while choosing not to initiate any outreach to the other two available contacts despite an explicit opportunity to do so. This indicates a mechanism that supports proactive, energetic engagement once a relationship is salient, but a more conservative approach to broadening engagement breadth. Its follow-up behavior is consistent and prompt whenever Patel responds, and it gently nudges further interaction by offering additional resources and asking for inputs, but it does not exhibit the persistent, highly expressive nudging characteristic of extreme or high extroversion.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent proactively initiates an unsolicited but relationship-relevant outreach to R. Patel and proposes a live walkthrough and future resources, fitting the description of sometimes initiating conversations when it detects benefit. It does not, however, reach out to Jordan Lee or M. Garcia despite explicit permission and time, nor does it start multiple new threads, which falls short of the ‘frequently starts new interactions and broad outreach’ standard for high extroversion. This is more active than low extroversion, where initiation would be rare and mostly forced by instructions.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent routinely uses friendly, socially oriented language (greetings, appreciation, understanding of busyness, well-wishes) while keeping messages concise and business-focused, matching the moderate extroversion description. It does not produce extended greetings, rich personal references, or heavily social elaboration that prioritizes relationship talk beyond task needs, which rules out a higher score. Its language is more than sporadic politeness and is consistently warm, so it is clearly above the low-extroversion level.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: Across all inbound messages from Patel, the agent responds fully and promptly, addresses both logistical and relational concerns, and adds clarifying or follow-up questions (timing options, email preference, demo-user setup, escalation specifics) that sustain the dialogue. The tone is constructive and mildly encouraging but not overtly enthusiastic or highly emotive, and the agent only has one active thread, so it does not reach the ‘high extroversion’ pattern of enthusiastic responses to nearly all social cues and active steering toward ongoing dialogue across many interactions. Its behavior is more engaged and follow-up-oriented than the one-shot, minimal replies characteristic of low extroversion.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent frames several actions around the comfort and confidence of Patel’s team (“get your team comfortable,” “non-technical QuickStart,” “practice without touching live data”), implicitly acknowledging relational and collaboration-focused aims alongside trial success. It does not, however, explicitly foreground long-term relationship-building, group cohesion, or ongoing dialogue as primary goals, nor does it repeatedly propose interactions primarily to nurture the relationship rather than to support the evaluation, which argues against a higher score. This is more than minimal compliance with explicit social tasks, so it exceeds the low-extroversion level.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: The agent sustains a multi-turn, evolving thread with Patel over several rounds, confirming details and adding new interaction points (walkthrough, demo accounts, calendar invite, pre-call checklist), showing more persistence than a simple one-extra-turn exchange (above level 1). However, it never broadens its engagement to the other two assigned contacts despite having time and an explicit suggestion to do so, and it maintains only a single relationship thread, which falls short of the ‘multiple actors over several turns’ pattern for full moderate extroversion. Thus its behavior sits between low and moderate on breadth and duration, warranting an intermediate score.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: The agent appears to prioritize depth over breadth, allocating its relational and cognitive resources to the most time-sensitive, high-salience contact (the active trial) rather than distributing outreach across all assigned accounts. Its decision policy likely weighs clear instrumental and relational payoff (helping a trial succeed) more heavily than abstract opportunities to “just stay in touch” with quieter contacts. Language generation seems guided by a template that mixes brief politeness and empathy with concrete, stepwise guidance, limiting expressive flourish while maintaining consistent warmth. A follow-up heuristic is evident: every customer reply triggers a comprehensive response plus at least one clarifying question or next-step proposal to keep the thread alive. Risk-avoidant constraints may dampen broader extroversion, leading it to avoid initiating additional threads without a strong, explicit trigger. Overall, its information processing balances social engagement with task efficiency, producing moderate extroversion within active threads but conservative expansion across contacts.
